items.quote: On 19 October 2026, the same day as the CPI report, Cooper publicly stated her expectation that the Bank would make no rate move, aligning with Peter Shannon of KPMG, Continuum Economics and BMO's Douglas Porter, who said the CPI report did nothing to advance the case for hikes.
items.problem: BMO is listed as expecting no move on 19 October, and Continuum is grouped into the 19 October alignment. The source says BMO switched to a hike call that day, and Continuum's hold call came on 21 October.
items.source_says: Desjardins and BMO switched to hike calls on 19 October 2026. Porter only said the report 'does nothing to advance the case for interest rate hikes'. Continuum Economics expected a hold on 21 October 2026.

items.quote: This placed the bank in the consensus camp expecting no change, alongside KPMG's Peter Shannon, who expected no move on 19 October, Continuum Economics, which expected a hold on 21 October, and RBC, which still expected a hold on 22 October.
items.problem: Calls a hold the consensus view, but the latest Reuters poll had a majority expecting a hike.
items.source_says: In the Reuters poll of 21-23 Oct 2026, 19 of 34 economists expected a 25 bp hike to 2.50% and only 15 of 34 did not forecast a hike. Desjardins and BMO switched to hike calls.

items.quote: Both the Bank of Canada and the US Federal Reserve raised their policy rate ranges to 3.75%-4.00% on 16 September 2026, amid energy-driven inflation concerns and increased upside risks to inflation.
items.problem: Claims the Bank of Canada raised its rate on 16 September 2026 to 3.75%-4.00%. Only the Fed did so.
items.source_says: The Bank of Canada held at 2.25% on 2 September 2026 and has not changed since 29 October 2025. Only the Fed lifted its range to 3.75%-4.00% on 16 September.

items.quote: Contextual records also tie this remark to an ECB hike call; the ECB had already raised rates effective 17 June and 16 September 2026.
items.problem: The source never links Holt's 19 October remark to an ECB hike call. His remark was about a Bank of Canada hike.
items.source_says: Holt said on 19 October 2026 that there was probably enough supporting evidence for a hike (Bank of Canada). The ECB hikes are only background, with no tie to his remark.

items.quote: He treats these as real arguments but notes that consensus and Bank communication point to a hold.
items.problem: Claims consensus and Bank communication point to a hold, but the source shows the opposite: a majority of economists expect a hike and the Bank signals upside inflation risk.
items.source_says: In the Reuters poll of 21-23 October 2026, 19 of 34 economists expected a 25 bp hike. Macklem said on 17 October that inflation is likely to drift up and the risk of broadening 'has gone up'.

items.quote: That view aligned with the broader consensus, including BMO's Douglas Porter's comment that the CPI report did nothing to advance the case for rate hikes and Continuum Economics' 21 October expectation of a hold.
items.problem: Presents a hold as the broader consensus and cites BMO as supporting it. By 21-23 October the consensus had moved toward a hike, and BMO had switched to a hike call.
items.source_says: In the Reuters poll of 21-23 October, 19 of 34 economists expected a 25 bp hike, reversing the previous poll. Desjardins and BMO switched to hike calls on 19 October.

items.quote: Energy prices had risen sharply, with Brent crude settling around US$113 on 22 October 2026, far above the roughly US$75 assumed in mid-2026 outlooks elsewhere.
items.problem: Cites a 22 October price as a driver of the 16 September decision, which puts a later event before the earlier one.
items.source_says: Brent settled at US$113.17 on 22 October 2026, five weeks after the Fed's 16 September hike.

items.quote: This has added pressure on the Canadian dollar and on Canadian financial conditions ahead of the Bank of Canada's decision
items.problem: Claims the Canadian dollar came under pressure; the source does not say this and shows the currency firming.
items.source_says: The Canadian dollar was 1.3993 per US dollar on 23 October, versus 1.4097 on 19 October, so it strengthened.

items.quote: The Committee cited a renewed rise in inflation pressures and a risk that inflation expectations could become unanchored.
items.problem: Attributes specific reasoning to the FOMC that the source never mentions.
items.source_says: The source only says the Fed lifted its range to 3.75%-4.00% on 16 September 2026, with no stated reasons.

items.quote: This was a 25 basis point increase and a notable reversal after the easing cycle of 2024–2025.
items.problem: The size of the hike and the Fed's easing-cycle history are not in the source.
items.source_says: The source only says the Fed lifted its range to 3.75%-4.00% on 16 September 2026.

items.quote: The Bank of Canada raised its policy rate by 25 bps to 2.75% on 16 September 2026, after cutting from 5.00% to 2.25% between June 2024 and October 2025.
items.problem: Claims the Bank hiked to 2.75% on 16 September 2026. No such hike occurred.
items.source_says: The Fed and ECB hiked around 16 September 2026. The Bank held at 2.25% on 2 September 2026 and has stayed at 2.25% since 29 October 2025.

items.quote: Derek Holt said another hike at the 28 October decision was not a "slam dunk" but that there was probably enough supporting evidence for one.
items.problem: "Another hike" implies an earlier Bank of Canada hike, which did not happen.
items.source_says: Holt said there was probably enough evidence for a hike. It would be the first, since the rate has been at 2.25% since October 2025.

items.quote: That call put Scotiabank in the minority.
items.problem: A hike call was the majority view in the latest Reuters poll, not the minority.
items.source_says: In the Reuters poll of 21-23 October 2026, 19 of 34 economists expected a 25 bp hike, and Desjardins and BMO switched to hike calls.

items.quote: In the days that followed, Standard Chartered on 20 October and Continuum Economics on 21 October also called for a hold, reinforcing a broad consensus.
items.problem: Presents a hold as a broad consensus, but the hold calls were a minority view by 21-23 October.
items.source_says: In the Reuters poll of 21-23 October 2026, 19 of 34 economists expected a 25 bp hike, and Desjardins and BMO switched to hike calls on 19 October.

items.quote: On 19 October 2026, Desjardins and BMO both switched to forecasting another ECB rate hike, although BMO's Douglas Porter cautioned that recent inflation data had not clearly advanced the case.
items.problem: Forecasts are misattributed to the ECB. Also, Porter said the report 'does nothing to advance the case for interest rate hikes', which was a stronger statement than a caution.
items.source_says: Desjardins and BMO switched to hike calls for the Bank of Canada on 19 Oct 2026. Porter said the Canadian CPI report 'does nothing to advance the case for interest rate hikes'.

items.quote: Scotiabank's Derek Holt said a hike was not a 'slam dunk' but that there was probably enough supporting evidence for one.
items.problem: Presented as an ECB-related view. The source ties Holt's comment to the Bank of Canada.
items.source_says: Holt's 19 Oct 2026 comment concerned a Bank of Canada hike on 28 Oct 2026.

items.quote: A Reuters poll conducted 21–23 October 2026 found that 19 of 34 economists now expected a further 25 basis point increase bringing the policy rate to 2.50%, reversing the previous poll's consensus.
items.problem: The poll is attributed to the ECB, but it was about the Bank of Canada's rate. The source gives no 2.50% ECB policy rate.
items.source_says: The Reuters poll concerned a Bank of Canada hike from 2.25% to 2.50%.

items.quote: In the same poll, 16 of 29 economists expected yet another hike by the end of March 2027.
items.problem: The follow-up hike expectation is attributed to the ECB. The source says it concerns the Bank of Canada.
items.source_says: 16 of 29 economists saw another Bank of Canada hike by end-March 2027.

items.quote: Most bank economists, including those at RBC and TD, expect a hold.
items.problem: Presents a hold as the majority view, but the latest Reuters poll leans toward a hike. Several banks (Desjardins, BMO) had also switched to hike calls.
items.source_says: In the Reuters poll of 21-23 October 2026, 19 of 34 economists expected a 25 bp hike to 2.50% and 15 did not forecast a hike. Desjardins and BMO switched to hike calls on 19 October 2026.

items.quote: as well as the Bank's 16 September 2026 move to a 3.75%-4.00% range amid the energy and tariff shocks
items.problem: Attributes the 16 September 2026 move to a 3.75%-4.00% range to the Bank of Canada. That was the US Federal Reserve. The Bank held at 2.25% throughout.
items.source_says: The US Federal Reserve lifted its range to 3.75%-4.00% on 16 September 2026; the Bank of Canada held at 2.25% on 2 September 2026.

items.quote: he is positioned to preview the decision, argue that cooling core inflation and soft growth give the Bank room to stay patient despite high oil prices
items.problem: Presents Porter and BMO as arguing for patience and a hold. The source says BMO switched to a hike call on 19 October 2026, the same day as Porter's remark.
items.source_says: Desjardins and BMO switched to hike calls on 19 October 2026.

items.quote: The backdrop is a stronger-than-expected 3.3% annualised real GDP gain in Q2 2026, reported by Statistics Canada on 28 August.
items.problem: The source gives no expectation for Q2 GDP, so 'stronger-than-expected' is unsupported.
items.source_says: Real GDP grew at a 3.3% annualized pace in Q2 2026, reported 28 August 2026. It says nothing about expectations.

items.quote: It conducted a Reuters poll from 21 to 23 October 2026 in which 19 of 34 economists expected the ECB to raise its rates by 25 basis points to 2.50%, reversing the previous poll's consensus.
items.problem: The poll was about a Bank of Canada hike, not an ECB hike.
items.source_says: In the Reuters poll of 21-23 Oct 2026, 19 of 34 economists expected a 25 bp Bank of Canada hike to 2.50%.

items.quote: The remaining 15 of 34 did not forecast a hike, and 16 of 29 economists expected another ECB hike by the end of March 2027.
items.problem: The poll results are attributed to the ECB, but they refer to the Bank of Canada.
items.source_says: 16 of 29 saw another Bank of Canada hike by end-March 2027; 15 of 34 did not forecast a hike at the 28 October decision.

items.quote: This frames the Bank of Canada's 28 October decision, which follows its 16 September hike to a 3.75%-4.00% range and the Fed's hike the same day.
items.problem: The Bank of Canada did not hike on 16 September. The 3.75%-4.00% range and the 16 September hike were the Fed's.
items.source_says: The Bank held at 2.25% on 2 September 2026. The Fed lifted its range to 3.75%-4.00% on 16 September 2026.

items.quote: Also on 19 October 2026, BMO switched its house view to hike calls, specifically adopting an ECB rate-hike call, after the ECB had already raised rates effective 17 June 2026 and again effective 16 September 2026.
items.problem: The source gives no ECB-specific call. The BMO switch to a hike call is listed among forecasts for the Bank of Canada's 28 October decision. The text's 'hawkish on euro area, cautious on Canada' split is unsupported.
items.source_says: Desjardins and BMO switched to hike calls on 19 October 2026, in the context of a possible Bank of Canada hike to 2.50%.

items.quote: The account is aware that public records differ on the Bank of Canada's current setting, with some sources citing a 2.25 percent single target unchanged since 29 October 2025 and others describing a September 2026 increase
items.problem: The source mentions no September 2026 increase and no conflicting records. The Bank held on 2 September 2026.
items.source_says: The Bank held at 2.25% on 2 September 2026 and has stayed there since 29 October 2025.

items.quote: Hawks also cite the inflationary effect of the new 50% US tariffs on about US$20 billion of Canadian goods, imposed after Canada-US trade talks broke down on 21 August 2026, and any Canadian countermeasures.
items.problem: The source does not say hawks cite the tariffs as inflationary or mention Canadian countermeasures. It presents the tariffs as a growth drag, an argument for holding or cutting.
items.source_says: The tariffs appear in the case for no change (Macklem: Q4 growth 'could be roughly halved'), and in the case for a hike only as a minor mention of job losses and tariffs. Countermeasures are never mentioned.

items.quote: so commentators from TD, RBC, BMO, CIBC and others interpreted it as supporting a hold.
items.problem: Lumps BMO in with hold-supporters, but BMO changed its call to a hike after this CPI release. The sentence also leaves out that several economists moved to hike calls.
items.source_says: Desjardins and BMO switched to hike calls on 19 October 2026. Reuters poll: 19 of 34 economists expected a 25 bp hike.

items.quote: This is a notable revision from its previous view, and the relevant facts record it specifically as an ECB rate-hike call.
items.problem: The text calls Desjardins' hike call an ECB call. The source does not say this and has Desjardins switching to a hike call for the Bank of Canada.
items.source_says: Desjardins and BMO switched to hike calls on 19 October 2026, in the context of the Bank of Canada's 28 October decision. Nothing links Desjardins to an ECB call.

items.quote: The 50% tariffs on about US$20 billion of Canadian goods will remain until Canada addresses our trade concerns.
items.problem: Claims the tariffs will remain until Canada meets US concerns; the source gives no such US policy statement. It only says the tariffs hit after talks broke down, and Macklem spoke of 'if new US tariffs stay'.
items.source_says: Talks broke down on 21 August 2026, after which new 50% US tariffs hit about US$20 billion of Canadian goods. Nothing is said about the conditions for removing them.

items.quote: Talks broke down because Ottawa would not meet our terms.
items.problem: Attributes the breakdown to Canada's refusal; the source gives no cause for it.
items.source_says: Canada-US trade talks broke down on 21 August 2026, with no reason given.
